reason: The css grammar leaves @charset strings and keyframe percentage selectors unscoped; treesitter captures them as strings and numbers.
Quotes of the unscoped @charset string. Follows the entry above.

Plain property values are support.constant.property-value in TextMate. nvim-treesitter gives (plain_value) no capture, and adding one would recolor every other colorscheme that has these queries on its runtimepath.
Keyframe names are variable.parameter.keyframe-list in TextMate. The css query captures them with the same @variable as custom properties, which the theme paints green.
Entity punctuation. The html query captures the whole & reference as one @character.special node.
The doctype is one (doctype) node in tree-sitter-html. TextMate splits DOCTYPE from the html attribute.
The ecma query marks document, window and console as @variable.builtin alongside this. TextMate scopes only this and super as variable.language.
Regex flags are keyword.other in TextMate. tree-sitter-javascript captures the whole literal including flags as @string.regexp.
Known DOM properties are support.variable.property in TextMate, which no rule colors. Treesitter cannot tell length from a user property.
The ecma query marks console as @variable.builtin, which adds the variable.language italic. Color matches.
Same console heuristic inside a fenced JavaScript block.
JSON Key Level 1 color. TextMate colors keys by nesting depth; treesitter has one @property capture.
JSON Key Level 2 color. Same depth limitation.
JSON Key Level 3 color. Same depth limitation.
The json query conceals an escaped quote with the same @conceal capture as string quotes, so it takes the punctuation grey instead of the escape color.
tree-sitter-json's escape_sequence node covers only the backslash and u, while TextMate scopes the whole \u00e9.
The Lua TextMate grammar scopes some identifiers as variable.other and leaves others unscoped depending on position. Treesitter captures them all as @variable.
The Lua grammar scopes the object of a method definition or call as entity.name.class. Treesitter sees an ordinary variable.
The Lua grammar scopes the table in `function M.new` as part of the function name.
The Lua grammar includes the dot of `string.format` in the support.function scope.
The lua query captures in and goto with the generic @keyword that also covers local, which the theme paints purple. keyword.control.lua is grey.
LuaDoc tags inside comments. The luadoc parser is not installed, so the whole comment is @comment.
LuaDoc parameter name inside a comment. See the @param entry.
LuaDoc type inside a comment. See the @param entry.
Bold delimiters inside bold-italic text. Treesitter combines the italic flag from the enclosing emphasis; the theme's bold-italic rule is bold only.
Bold text nested in italic, or the reverse. Treesitter combines both flags; the theme's bold-italic rule is bold only.
Italic delimiters nested inside bold. Treesitter applies the inner italic flag.
The heading marker is punctuation.definition.heading in TextMate. The markdown query captures marker and text as one @markup.heading node.
Link title quotes. The markdown_inline query captures the quoted title as one @markup.link.label node.
Link titles are string.other.link.description.title in TextMate. The markdown_inline query uses the same @markup.link.label as link text.
Image descriptions are string.other.link.description in TextMate. The markdown_inline query uses the same @markup.link.label as link text.
Image brackets carry no punctuation scope in TextMate, unlike link brackets.
Image destination parentheses. The markdown_inline query gives them no capture.
Reference definition brackets are punctuation in TextMate. The markdown query captures the whole label including brackets.
The shortcut reference label [ref] is constant.other.reference.link in TextMate. The markdown_inline query captures it as link punctuation.
The checked task marker. The markdown query captures [x] as one @markup.list.checked node.
Fence delimiters are punctuation in TextMate. The markdown query gives the whole fenced block @markup.raw.block.
Autolink angle brackets. The markdown_inline query includes them in the @markup.link.url capture.
Thematic breaks are meta.separator in TextMate. The markdown query captures them with the same @punctuation.special as table pipes and quote markers.
String prefixes are storage.type.string in TextMate. tree-sitter-python puts the prefix inside the string_start node with the quote.
Inside a comprehension the Python grammar scopes in, is and not as control flow. The python query captures them as @keyword.operator like every other operator.
self in a parameter list is variable.parameter in TextMate. The python query applies @variable.builtin everywhere.
super and exception classes are support.type in TextMate. The python query captures them as builtin function calls.
The decorator marker. The python query captures @ and the decorator name as one @attribute node.
f-string quotes carry no punctuation scope in the VS Code grammar, unlike every other string.
Raw strings are string.regexp in TextMate. Treesitter sees an ordinary string.
Regex quantifier inside a raw string. See the raw string entry.
__name__ is support.variable.magic in TextMate, which no rule colors. The python query captures uppercase-looking names as @constant.
A computed method name in a class body. The TextMate grammar scopes it outside meta.block; the treesitter rule sees the class body ancestor.
The this return type is support.type.primitive in TextMate. The typescript query gives (this_type) no capture.
Empty arrow function parameter parentheses in TSX parse without a formal_parameters node that the extension rule can match.
